title: Contextual Visual Distinctiveness in Online Product Search
abstract: arXiv:2608.21691v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In online product search, returned alternatives often look alike. We investigate when a product's visual separation from its closest look-alike in a returned set increases its choice probability. We introduce two occasion-level constructs: contextual visual distinctiveness (image distance from the nearest similar alternative in the consideration set) and relative fit (compatibility with the search query). We hypothesize that distinctiveness favors selection and is highly contextual, yields a premium that rises with relative fit, and matters most when text descriptions fail to differentiate options. Analyzing over 800,000 e-commerce search events using dense representations, we apply search-event and product fixed effects to evaluate the exact same product alongside varying visual neighbors. translated_title: 在线产品搜索中的情境视觉独特性
translated_abstract: 在在线产品搜索中，返回的备选产品往往看起来相似。我们研究了当产品在返回集中与其最相似的近似品在视觉上分离时，是否会提高其被选择的概率。我们引入了两个情境层面的构念：情境视觉独特性（产品与考虑集中最近相似替代品的图像距离）和相对匹配度（与搜索查询的兼容性）。我们假设独特性有利于选择，且具有高度情境性，其带来的溢价随相对匹配度的提高而增加，并且在文本描述无法区分选项时最为重要。通过使用密集表示分析超过80万次电子商务搜索事件，我们应用搜索事件和产品固定效应来评估同一产品在不同视觉邻域下的表现。结果显示，当产品缺乏近似的相似品时，其被点击的可能性显著更高。这种独特性溢价随相对匹配度的提高而增加。
tldr: 这项研究发现，在线产品搜索中，产品在返回集中与最相似替代品的视觉差异（情境视觉独特性）能显著提高其被点击的概率，且这种优势在匹配度较高和文本描述无法区分选项时更为明显。
en_tdlr: This research finds that in online product search, a product's visual distinctiveness from its closest look-alike in the returned set significantly increases its click probability, with this premium growing with higher relative fit and when text descriptions fail to differentiate options.
